prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1348; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a reported low-speed collision in a parking lot. Insured states the other vehicle backed into the driver's side door while the insured was stopped. Insured reports feeling dizzy and having a headache at the scene and was transported to urgent care. Police report requested. Photos of both vehicles received and saved to file.

Entry 2: Claimant is represented by counsel. Letter of representation received. All further contact to be directed to the attorney's office. Claimant's attorney indicates a head injury with concussion diagnosis and states that medical records and billing will be forthcoming. Recorded that no recorded statement will be taken from the claimant without counsel present.

Entry 3: Medical authorization and records request sent to attorney's office. Records received from urgent care reflect a diagnosis of concussion, instructions for rest, and a follow-up referral to neurology. Treatment notes indicate ongoing symptoms including headaches and light sensitivity. Records under review.

Entry 4: Spoke with claimant's attorney regarding status of the neurology follow-up. Attorney confirms claimant has an appointment scheduled and will provide updated records after the visit. Attorney requested that the carrier not contact the claimant's employer. Noted in file. Reviewed property damage estimate for the claimant's vehicle; repair shop inspection is pending.

Entry 5: Reviewed available police report and photos. Report notes no citations issued and both drivers describe the vehicles as stationary or nearly so at impact. Liability investigation ongoing. Set diary to follow up with counsel on neurology records and repair inspection results. Claim remains open with injury component under evaluation.
